questions.q: What do the authors say about creativity?
a: It applies far beyond art and can be retrained like a muscle
It is a rare gift that only artists possess
It fades permanently once you reach adulthood
It matters mainly in artistic careers
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues everyone is born creative, that creativity is broader than art and can be rebuilt with practice.

questions.q: What did the MRI technician do to help children?
a: Turned the scanners into fun adventures like pirate ships
Built smaller machines for young patients
Played music during each scan
Let children operate the machine themselves
questions.why: The summary uses the technician who redesigned the scanner's look so children would feel safer inside it.

questions.q: What did the IBM survey of CEOs find?
a: Creativity was rated the most important leadership quality
Most CEOs valued analytical skills above all
Few companies were hiring creative staff
Creativity ranked below financial discipline
questions.why: Lesson 2 cites a survey in which over 1,500 CEOs named creativity the top leadership quality.

questions.q: What did Paul McCartney's story illustrate?
a: Creative people are often told to choose something practical
Fame comes only after years of failure
Music skills transfer easily to business
Schools should teach more art history
questions.why: The summary notes McCartney was urged to give up music for something more practical, and that this pressure still exists.

questions.q: What do the authors recommend for a satisfying career?
a: Balancing passion with enough income to live well
Choosing the highest-paying job available
Following passion regardless of what it pays
Avoiding creative work until you are financially secure
questions.why: Lesson 3 says pure passion rarely pays the bills and pure money makes you miserable, so balance is the answer.
